newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Lavipharm set for rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Greek Lavipharm set for rights issue.

text.p: Greek pharmaceuticals and cosmetics maker Lavipharm received shareholder approval for a 6.464 billion drachma ($23.6 million) rights issue on Tuesday.
Lavipharm announced a patch for acne treatment, a patented global innovation, and senior company officials also said group earnings were forecast to rise 21.4 percent in fiscal 1997.
The terms of the rights issue will be four new shares per 10 outstanding at 1,900 drachmas each, although management initially proposed a 2,000 drachma issue price.
The last cum-rights trading day will be June 30.

Proceeds will be used to complete capital investments for transdermal drug production and warehousing facilities, finance research and development in transdermal and osmotic technology and to retire bank debt and finance further acquisitions.
Company president Athanasios Lavidas announced the development of a "revolutionary" transdermal patch for acne treatment.
The new product was developed by Lavipharm's subsidiary Scherpa Transdermals, which has been renamed Lavipharm Laboratories.
Lavipharm acquired a 48 percent stake in New Jersey-based Scherpa Transdermals, an R&D laboratory, for 5.2 billion drachmas in late 1996.
Lavidas said the product turned in excellent results in field tests in the United States, treating acne in 36 hours.
Production of patches will start in the coming weeks in Greece and will be marketed internationally around September 1997 by distributor L'Oreal.

Lavipharm got shareholder approval for the issue of non-convertible, four-year drachma bonds totalling 5.0 billion drachmas which will be issued at three-month Athibor plus a maximum 2.5 percent spread.
In fiscal 1996, Lavipharm's pretax profit rose 22.1 percent to 2.636 billion drachmas on turnover growth of 40.5 percent to 44.254 billion.
Management told shareholders that group turnover in the first five months of 1997 was up 50 percent, versus a budgeted increase of 35 percent.
Asked by shareholders on earnings in 1997, Lavidas replied that no figures were available so far and that the next results announcement would come in the form of interim results.

But senior company officials told Reuters that group earnings were forecast to improve by 21.4 percent to 3.2 billion drachmas in fiscal 1997 on turnover growth of around 13 percent to 50 billion drachmas.
Lavipharm will distribute a dividend per share of 60 drachmas for fiscal 1996, up from 45 drachmas a year earlier.
Its shares will trade ex-dividend June 18 and dividend payments will start on June 30.
Lavipharm's shares firmed 45 drachmas to 2,450 on Tuesday in heavy volume of 68,860 shares.
